The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1912

    Alexander Nevsky Cathedral

    Alexander Pomerantsev designed it, and it was finished in 1912. It honours the Russian soldiers who died in the war of 1877–1878 that freed Bulgaria from Ottoman rule.

    Look for

    Go down to the crypt, which holds a large collection of Orthodox icons gathered from across Bulgaria.

  2. 02
    Landmark

    Ancient Serdica Complex

    Builders of the metro uncovered this part of Roman Serdica, and it opened as an open-air site in 2016. Emperor Constantine is said to have called the city his Rome.

  3. 03
    Building · 1576

    Banya Bashi Mosque

    Built in 1576 and attributed to the great architect Mimar Sinan, it is the only mosque still in use in Sofia. Its name refers to the thermal baths that once stood beside it.

    Look for

    Look around: the Sofia Synagogue, St Nedelya Church and the Catholic Cathedral of St Joseph all stand within a few minutes’ walk.

  4. 04
    Park

    Borisova Gradina

    Gardener Daniel Neff began planting it in the 1880s, and it is named after Tsar Boris III. The national stadium stands on its edge.

    Look for

    Near the middle of the park rises a tall obelisk, the Mound of Brotherhood, raised in 1956 to honour communist fighters.

  5. 05
    Church

    Boyana Church

    The frescoes, dated 1259, show unusually lifelike faces for their time. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

    Look for

    Find the portraits of the founders, Sebastocrator Kaloyan and his wife Desislava, painted with the care of real faces.

  6. 06
    Museum · 1913

    Central Mineral Baths

    Petko Momchilov and Friedrich Grünanger designed it, and it opened in 1913. Across the street, people still fill bottles with warm mineral water from public taps.

  7. 07
    Culture · 1906

    Ivan Vazov National Theatre

    The Viennese firm Fellner & Helmer designed it, and it opened in 1906. It is named after Ivan Vazov, the writer known as the patriarch of Bulgarian literature.

    Look for

    In the City Garden in front, chess players often gather around boards at the tables.

  8. 08
    Culture · 1981

    National Palace of Culture

    It opened in 1981 for the 1,300th anniversary of the Bulgarian state. The park in front is a favourite gathering place, with Vitosha mountain behind.

  9. 09
    Church

    Rotunda of St. George

    Built in the 4th century, it is the oldest standing building in Sofia. Layers of medieval frescoes survived its time as a mosque under Ottoman rule.

    Look for

    Behind the rotunda run the excavated remains of a Roman street and the foundations of other buildings of Serdica.

  10. 10
    Church · 1914

    Russian Church

    It was built for the Russian embassy and consecrated in 1914. In the crypt, visitors leave written wishes at the tomb of Archbishop Seraphim.

  11. 11
    Church

    St. Sofia Church

    The present church dates from the 6th century, on the site of older churches and a Roman cemetery. In the 14th century the city began to be called Sofia after it.

    Look for

    Beside the church, a bronze lion guards the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and its eternal flame.

  12. 12
    Shopping

    Vitosha Boulevard

    The boulevard runs from St. Nedelya Church towards the mountain that gives it its name. It is the city’s main promenade on summer evenings.

    Look for

    Two bronze lions guard the steps of the Palace of Justice, the grand courthouse that faces the boulevard.
